note: An opportunity is an actual observed key glyph in a lost try with a subsequent try in the same campaign. Picture recall and key identity are separate. Toward-cover means the first removal touches that observed key or its geometric cover ancestors. Strict straight means no removal outside that cover corridor before a previously seen key is re-exposed. This deliberately strict operational definition can penalize useful side clearance or tray relief; it is not a proof of shortest optimal play. Never seeing a key provides no memory opportunity. No bot or profile changed.

features.definition: Actual public key glyph visible in the overlay region; cumulative sightings on the stored winning route, in tile-removal moves. No-key boards use null for time-to-both, not zero.
